tagline: China's central crossroads — the rail hub nearest the Shaolin Temple, where monks perfected kung fu 1,500 years ago.
overview: Zhengzhou is the crossroads of China — the country's biggest rail junction, where north-south and east-west high-speed lines cross. It's a modern 12-million-person metropolis that few foreigners knew before Speed's 2025 stream.

The city's claim to fame is 80km away: the Shaolin Temple on Mount Song, where Buddhist monks have trained in kung fu since the 6th century — the world's most famous martial-arts monastery, and the site of Speed's legendary training session that went viral across platforms.

Zhengzhou itself is one of China's ancient capitals — the Shang dynasty built city walls here 3,600 years ago, and the Henan Museum holds bronzes and jades from the Yellow River's earliest civilisations.
